_note: Figures from the papers for the Budget Meeting of 26 February 2026. Each says what it is a count of and where it is printed. Page numbers are the printed pages of each document. src ids are in sources.json.

netBudget.what: the General Fund net budget for 2026/27 (the budget requirement)

ctRise.what: the total rise in the county council's share of council tax for 2026/27: 1.80% general council tax and 2.00% Adult Social Care precept
ctRise.at: recommendations vi and vii, p. 4; Table 7, p. 22

bandD.what: the county council's Band D council tax for 2026/27, up from £1,735.79 in 2025/26

bandA.what: the county council's Band A council tax for 2026/27, up £43.98 a year; 35% of chargeable properties in the county are in Band A

ctRequirement.what: the council tax cash needed, after grants, business rates and other income are taken from the budget requirement

taxBase.what: the council tax base, in Band D equivalent properties

onePercent.what: what each 1% of council tax raises

savings.what: the savings in the 2026/27 budget, earlier and new together

extraRsg.what: the additional Revenue Support Grant in 2026/27 from the final finance settlement (£1.999m in 2027/28), held in a Strategic Contingency

savingsContingency.what: the savings delivery contingency in the 2026/27 budget

reserve.what: the General Fund Unearmarked Reserve at 31 March 2026 and, as planned, at 31 March 2027

reservePolicy.what: the level of net revenue spending the council seeks to hold as its General Fund Unearmarked Reserve

noReserves.what: the use of reserves to balance the 2026/27 budget

s25reserves.text: the level of Reserves is currently adequate

s25robust.text: based on the best available information

lawful.text: a duty to facilitate, rather than obstruct, the setting of a lawful budget

deadline.text: a duty to set a budget before 1 March

amendStatement.text: makes no appreciable impact on the financial resilience of the Council
amendStatement.at: the Section 151 Officer's statement on each of Annexes 1 to 4

notice.text: Alternative budgets must be in final form, with the prior written approval of the Chief Financial Officer, at least five clear working days before the Budget meeting. Late ones are not allowed.

lawfulForm.text: A proposal that the Chief Financial Officer does not accept as capable of being adopted as a lawful budget is not allowed.

package.text: Each group's list of amendments is proposed, seconded, debated and voted on as if it were a single amendment.

circulate.text: The group leader decides when the Monitoring Officer shares the amendment with other councillors, but no later than the start of the meeting.

order.text: The Leader moves the Budget, then the other group leaders are called in order of group size.

reply.text: The proposer of an alternative budget has a right of reply, and so does the proposer of the Administration's Budget before each vote. Every vote is a recorded vote.

noNew.text: No new amendments once the debate returns to the substantive motion. The mover of the Budget replies last, for up to five minutes.

arrears.text: A member more than two months behind with council tax must say so and may not vote on the Budget. Failing to do so is a criminal offence.
arrears.at: Standing Order 4.9(j); Local Government Finance Act 1992, s.106

remote.text: A member attending remotely may be allowed to speak but may not vote.

recorded.text: There must be a recorded vote on decisions at the Budget meeting.

majority.text: Decided by a simple majority of members present and voting. On equal votes the Chair may use a casting vote; if not, the matter falls.

closure.text: A member who has not yet spoken may move that the question be now put; the Chair decides whether the matter has been sufficiently discussed.

billing.text: Standing Order 4.1 says the Budget meeting must be held before 11 March, the deadline for the district councils that send the bills; the Budget Report gives the county's own duty as before 1 March.
billing.at: Standing Order 4.1; Budget Report para. 78, p. 28
